WebFetch of code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks: UserPromptSubmit carries user_input + user_input_type ('user'|'system'); UserPromptExpansion carries command_name, user_input, expanded_prompt; stdout on exit 0 is injected as context on both
DEVIATIONS: Field names: the current Claude Code docs (fetched) give UserPromptSubmit's typed text as `user_input` with `user_input_type`, not `prompt`. The hook accepts user_input first and prompt (older releases) too, and refuses any turn whose user_input_type is not 'user' (Claude Code also fires UserPromptSubmit for turns it starts itself: task notices, scheduled prompts). It never reads `expanded_prompt` (the skill template).

Payload handoff: the hook stages stdin in a mktemp file (as policy-gate.sh does) instead of an env var (obs-capture.sh style): a prompt can exceed an env var (32K chars on Windows). A grep prefilter skips python for prompts naming neither command.

Continuing a run also needs the ticket to be fresh (per the lead's note), so every `checkctl run` checks it; the refusal names 'opening a ritual run' or 'continuing ritual <id>'. A consumed ticket's ts is also stored in memory-run.json (ticket_consumed), so a ticket file that survives deletion stays spent. memory-run.json records invoked_by, ticket_ts, ticket_skill and ticket_session.
Ticket validation beyond the contract: skill must be project-memory|adopt, ts must parse, a ts more than 5 min in the future is refused. Exit code on refusal is 1, like statectl's refusals.

Doctor ritual_ticket row: fresh -> OK with minutes left; absent with the hook wired -> OK 'none open'; expired/consumed -> OK naming it; unparsable or invalid -> WARN; hook missing or not wired -> WARN (no ticket can ever be minted). ritual-ticket.sh joined EXPECTED_HOOKS. This changed T6's test_secrets.TestDoctor.test_absent_features_skip_then_read_when_present on purpose: the fixture has no hook wired, so the absent row is WARN, and the 'present' half now grants a real ticket (its old {ts} ticket has no skill and is invalid).

Existing tests changed on purpose: test_contracts (two TestPublishTransaction tests) and test_secrets (TestGitScope run) call self.grant_ticket() before checkctl run; FixtureCase gained grant_ticket().

Session counter: counts distinct session ids in SessionStart events from the capture lane (spool minus ingest.jsonl, plus segments dated on/after the last ritual) after last_completed, plus the current session from the hook's own payload, minus the ritual's session (memory-run.json ticket_session). With SessionStart capture off the count is None: the nudge says 'sessions not counted' and goes by age alone. The hook still never writes the journal.

The ticket is gitignored: added to distctl's managed tracked block, the repo's .gitignore block, and checkctl._deliberately_ignored. Without it PUBLISH's `git add -A` would commit a ticket every ritual.
